sanskrit: amūrtarayasaḥ putro gayo rājarṣisattamaḥ puṇyāni yasya karmāṇi tāni me śṛṇu bhārata
english: The son of Amūrtarayas was Gaya, that best of royal sages; hear from me, O Bhārata, of his meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: yasya yajño babhūveha bahvanno bahudakṣiṇaḥ yatrānnaparvatā rājañ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: His sacrifice here was one of abundant food and rich fees; at it, O king, there were mountains of food by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: ghṛtakulyāś ca dadhnaś ca nadyo bahuśatās tathā vyañjanānāṃ pravāhāś ca mahārhāṇāṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: There were streams of clarified butter and rivers of curds by the hundreds, and flows of condiments of great worth by the thousands.

sanskrit: ahany ahani cāpy etad yācatāṃ saṃpradīyate anyat tu brāhmaṇā rājan bhuñjate 'nnaṃ susaṃskṛtam
english: Day after day all this was given to those who asked; and beyond that, O king, the brahmins partook of food excellently prepared.

sanskrit: tatra vai dakṣiṇākāle brahmaghoṣo divaṃ gataḥ na sma prajñāyate kiṃ cid brahmaśabdena bhārata
english: At the time of the sacrificial fees, the chanting of the Veda rose up to heaven; nothing whatsoever could be distinguished through the noise of the Veda, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: puṇyena caratā rājan bhūr diśaḥ khaṃ nabhas tathā āpūrṇam āsīc chabdena tad apy āsīn mahādbhutam
english: As that meritorious king moved about, the earth, the directions, the sky, and the heavens were filled with the sound — and that too was a great wonder.

sanskrit: tatra sma gāthā gāyanti manuṣyā bharatarṣabha annapānaiḥ śubhais tṛptā deśe deśe suvarcasaḥ
english: There men of radiant glory, satisfied with auspicious food and drink, sang songs in every region, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: gayasya yajñe ke tv adya prāṇino bhoktum īpsavaḥ yatra bhojanaśiṣṭasya parvatāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ
english: "Who are the living beings today that desire to eat at Gaya's sacrifice, where twenty-five mountains remain as the leftover of the feast?"

sanskrit: na sma pūrve janāś cakrur na kariṣyanti cāpare gayo yad akarod yajñe rājarṣir amitadyutiḥ
english: Neither did the people before nor will those after accomplish what Gaya, the royal sage of boundless splendour, did at his sacrifice.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu devā haviṣā gayena paritarpitāḥ punaḥ śakṣyanty upādātum anyair dattāni kāni cit
english: How indeed could the gods, fully satisfied with the oblations offered by Gaya, ever again accept whatever may be given by others?

sanskrit: evaṃvidhāḥ subahavas tasya yajñe mahātmanaḥ babhūvur asya sarasaḥ samīpe kurunandana
english: Many such wonders as these occurred at the sacrifice of that great-souled one near his lake, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ saṃprasthito rājā kaunteyo bhūridakṣiṇaḥ agastyāśramam āsādya durjayāyām uvāsa ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king, son of Kuntī, he of abundant largesse, set out and, reaching the hermitage of Agastya, took up residence at Durjayā.

sanskrit: tatra vai lomaśaṃ rājā papraccha vadatāṃ varaḥ agastyeneha vātāpiḥ kimartham upaśāmitaḥ
english: There the king, best among speakers, asked Lomaśa: "For what reason was Vātāpi here quelled by Agastya?"

sanskrit: āsīd vā kiṃprabhāvaś ca sa daityo mānavāntakaḥ kimarthaṃ codgato manyur agastyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "What power had that daitya, the destroyer of men? And why did the wrath of the great-souled Agastya arise?"

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca ilvalo nāma daiteya āsīt kauravanandana maṇimatyāṃ puri purā vātāpis tasya cānujaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: There was a daitya named Ilvala, O joy of the Kurus, and in the city of Maṇimatī of old, Vātāpi was his younger brother.

sanskrit: sa brāhmaṇaṃ tapoyuktam uvāca ditinandanaḥ putraṃ me bhagavān ekam indratulyaṃ prayacchatu
english: That son of Diti said to a brahmin possessed of austerities: "May the reverend one grant me a single son equal to Indra."

sanskrit: tasmai sa brāhmaṇo nādāt putraṃ vāsavasaṃmitam cukrodha so 'suras tasya brāhmaṇasya tato bhṛśam
english: The brahmin did not grant him a son equal to Vāsava; thereupon that asura became exceedingly wrathful toward that brahmin.

sanskrit: samāhvayati yaṃ vācā gataṃ vaivasvatakṣayam sa punar deham āsthāya jīvan sma pratidṛśyate
english: Whomever he called out to by name, even one who had gone to the abode of Vivasvat's son, would appear again alive, having reassumed a body.

sanskrit: tato vātāpim asuraṃ chāgaṃ kṛtvā susaṃskṛtam taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayitvā punar eva samāhvayat
english: Then, turning the asura Vātāpi into a goat and having it well prepared, he fed it to that brahmin and then called out to him again.

sanskrit: tasya pārśvaṃ vinirbhidya brāhmaṇasya mahāsuraḥ vātāpiḥ prahasan rājan niścakrāma viśāṃ pate
english: Tearing through the side of that brahmin, the great asura Vātāpi came out laughing, O king, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa brāhmaṇān rājan bhojayitvā punaḥ punaḥ hiṃsayām āsa daiteya ilvalo duṣṭacetanaḥ
english: In this way, O king, the daitya Ilvala, of wicked mind, repeatedly fed the brahmins and then slew them.

sanskrit: agastyaś cāpi bhagavān etasmin kāla eva tu pitṝn dadarśa garte vai lambamānān adhomukhān
english: And the venerable Agastya too, at precisely that time, saw his ancestors hanging head downward in a pit.

sanskrit: so 'pṛcchal lambamānāṃs tān bhavanta iha kiṃparāḥ saṃtānahetor iti te tam ūcur brahmavādinaḥ
english: He asked those hanging ones: "What is your condition here?" — inquiring for the sake of lineage; and they, expounders of the Veda, spoke to him.

sanskrit: te tasmai kathayām āsur vayaṃ te pitaraḥ svakāḥ gartam etam anuprāptā lambāmaḥ prasavārthinaḥ
english: They told him: "We are your own ancestors; we have descended into this pit and hang here, desiring offspring."

sanskrit: yadi no janayethās tvam agastyāpatyam uttamam syān no 'smān nirayān mokṣas tvaṃ ca putrāpnuyā gatim
english: "If you were to beget upon us a noble descendant of Agastya, we would be released from this hell, and you yourself would attain the goal by having a son."

sanskrit: sa tān uvāca tejasvī satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ kariṣye pitaraḥ kāmaṃ vyetu vo mānaso jvaraḥ
english: That splendid one, devoted to truth and righteousness, said to them: "I shall fulfil your wish, O ancestors; let the fever of your minds depart."

sanskrit: tataḥ prasavasaṃtānaṃ cintayan bhagavān ṛṣiḥ ātmanaḥ prasavasyārthe nāpaśyat sadṛśīṃ striyam
english: Then the venerable sage, reflecting on begetting a lineage, found no woman suitable for his own procreation.

sanskrit: sa tasya tasya sattvasya tat tad aṅgam anuttamam saṃbhṛtya tatsamair aṅgair nirmame striyam uttamām
english: He collected the choicest limb of each creature, and with limbs to match from each he fashioned a supreme woman.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ vidarbharājāya putrakāmāya tāmyate nirmitām ātmano 'rthāya muniḥ prādān mahātapāḥ
english: The sage of great austerity gave that woman, fashioned for his own purpose, to the king of Vidarbha who was anguished in his longing for a son.

sanskrit: sā tatra jajñe subhagā vidyutsaudāminī yathā vibhrājamānā vapusā vyavardhata śubhānanā
english: She was born there, the blessed one, radiant as a streak of lightning; shining with her form, she grew up, she of beautiful face.

sanskrit: jātamātrāṃ ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vaidarbhaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ praharṣeṇa dvijātibhyo nyavedayata bhārata
english: And seeing her the moment she was born, the lord of the earth of Vidarbha, with great joy, announced her to the twice-born, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: abhyanandanta tāṃ sarve brāhmaṇā vasudhādhipa lopāmudreti tasyāś ca cakrire nāma te dvijāḥ
english: All the brahmins rejoiced at her, O lord of the earth; and those twice-born ones gave her the name Lopāmudrā.

sanskrit: vavṛdhe sā mahārāja bibhratī rūpam uttamam apsv ivotpalinī śīghram agner iva śikhā śubhā
english: She grew up, O great king, bearing a supreme beauty — swiftly like a lotus in water, like the auspicious flame of fire.

sanskrit: tāṃ yauvanasthāṃ rājendra śataṃ kanyāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ dāśīśataṃ ca kalyāṇīm upatasthur vaśānugāḥ
english: When she had come to youth, O king of kings, a hundred maidens well adorned and a hundred maidservants waited upon that lovely one, obedient to her will.

sanskrit: sā sma dāsīśatavṛtā madhye kanyāśatasya ca āste tejasvinī kanyā rohiṇīva divi prabho
english: Surrounded by a hundred maidservants and seated among a hundred maidens, the radiant girl shone like Rohiṇī in the sky, O lord.

sanskrit: yauvanasthām api ca tāṃ śīlācārasamanvitām na vavre puruṣaḥ kaś cid bhayāt tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Though she was come to youth and endowed with good character and conduct, no man chose her out of fear of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: sā tu satyavatī kanyā rūpeṇāpsaraso 'py ati toṣayām āsa pitaraṃ śīlena svajanaṃ tathā
english: But that true-natured maiden, surpassing even the apsarases in beauty, pleased her father and likewise her kinsmen with her conduct.

sanskrit: vaidarbhīṃ tu tathāyuktāṃ yuvatīṃ prekṣya vai pitā manasā cintayām āsa kasmai dadyāṃ sutām iti
english: Seeing the maiden of Vidarbha thus endowed with every virtue, her father thought in his mind: "To whom shall I give my daughter?"

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca yadā tv amanyatāgastyo gārhasthye tāṃ kṣamām iti tadābhigamya provāca vaidarbhaṃ pṛthivīpatim
english: Lomaśa said: When Agastya concluded that she was fit for householder life, he went and spoke to the lord of the earth of Vidarbha.

sanskrit: rājan niveśe buddhir me vartate putrakāraṇāt varaye tvāṃ mahīpāla lopāmudrāṃ prayaccha me
english: "O king, my mind tends toward settled household life for the sake of offspring; I ask this of you, O protector of the earth — give me Lopāmudrā."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa muninā mahīpālo vicetanaḥ pratyākhyānāya cāśaktaḥ pradātum api naicchata
english: Addressed thus by the sage, the lord of the earth was bewildered — unable to refuse yet unwilling to give.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhāryām abhyetya provāca pṛthivīpatiḥ maharṣir vīryavān eṣa kruddhaḥ śāpāgninā dahet
english: Then the lord of the earth went to his wife and said: "This great and powerful sage, if angered, would burn us with the fire of his curse."

sanskrit: taṃ tathā duḥkhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sabhāryaṃ pṛthivīpatim lopāmudrābhigamyedaṃ kāle vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing the lord of the earth thus distressed together with his wife, Lopāmudrā approached at the right moment and spoke these words.

sanskrit: na matkṛte mahīpāla pīḍām abhyetum arhasi prayaccha mām agastyāya trāhy ātmānaṃ mayā pitaḥ
english: "O protector of the earth, you should not suffer distress on my account; give me to Agastya — save yourself through me, O father."

sanskrit: duhitur vacanād rājā so 'gastyāya mahātmane lopāmudrāṃ tataḥ prādād vidhipūrvaṃ viśāṃ pate
english: At his daughter's word, the king then gave Lopāmudrā to the great-souled Agastya according to proper rite, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: prāpya bhāryām agastyas tu lopāmudrām abhāṣata mahārhāṇy utsṛjaitāni vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca
english: Having received his wife, Agastya addressed Lopāmudrā: "Set aside these precious garments and ornaments."

sanskrit: tataḥ sā darśanīyāni mahārhāṇi tanūni ca samutsasarja rambhorūr vasanāny āyatekṣaṇā
english: Then she of lovely thighs and long eyes put off those beautiful, precious, fine garments.

sanskrit: tataś cīrāṇi jagrāha valkalāny ajināni ca samānavratacaryā ca babhūvāyatalocanā
english: And then the long-eyed one took up bark garments, bast-cloth, and deer-skins, and became one who followed the same vow and practice as he.

sanskrit: gaṅgādvāram athāgamya bhagavān ṛṣisattamaḥ ugram ātiṣṭhata tapaḥ saha patnyānukūlayā
english: Then the venerable sage, best of seers, came to Gaṅgādvāra and undertook severe austerities together with his devoted wife.

sanskrit: sā prītyā bahumānāc ca patiṃ paryacarat tadā agastyaś ca parāṃ prītiṃ bhāryāyām akarot prabhuḥ
english: She then served her husband with love and great respect; and Agastya, the lord, cherished supreme affection toward his wife.

sanskrit: tato bahutithe kāle lopāmudrāṃ viśāṃ pate tapasā dyotitāṃ snātāṃ dadarśa bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Then after a long time, O lord of the people, the venerable sage saw Lopāmudrā radiant with austerity and bathed in her season.

sanskrit: sa tasyāḥ paricāreṇa śaucena ca damena ca śriyā rūpeṇa ca prīto maithunāyājuhāva tām
english: Pleased by her devoted service, her purity, her self-restraint, her grace, and her beauty, he summoned her for conjugal union.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā prāñjalir bhūtvā lajjamāneva bhāminī tadā sapraṇayaṃ vākyaṃ bhagavantam athābravīt
english: Then she, the passionate one, joining her palms as if embarrassed, spoke these words to the venerable one with affectionate longing.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ prajāhetor bhāryāṃ patir avindata yā tu tvayi mama prītis tām ṛṣe kartum arhasi
english: "Without doubt a husband obtains a wife for the sake of progeny; the love that I have for you, O sage, you should reciprocate."

sanskrit: yathā pitur gṛhe vipra prāsāde śayanaṃ mama tathāvidhe tvaṃ śayane mām upaitum ihārhasi
english: "As I had a bed in a palace in my father's house, O brahmin — on such a bed you should come to me here."

sanskrit: icchāmi tvāṃ sragviṇaṃ ca bhūṣaṇaiś ca vibhūṣitam upasartuṃ yathākāmaṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitā
english: "I desire to approach you freely — you adorned with a garland and decorated with ornaments — I myself adorned with divine jewels."

sanskrit: agastya uvāca na vai dhanāni vidyante lopāmudre tathā mama yathāvidhāni kalyāṇi pitus tava sumadhyame
english: Agastya said: "O Lopāmudrā, O fair-waisted one, I do not have wealth of the kind befitting your father's house, O auspicious one."

sanskrit: lopāmudrovāca īśo 'si tapasā sarvaṃ samāhartum iheśvara kṣaṇena jīvaloke yad vasu kiṃ cana vidyate
english: Lopāmudrā said: "You are capable, O lord, of gathering through your austerities in an instant all the wealth that exists in the living world."

sanskrit: agastya uvāca evam etad yathāttha tvaṃ tapovyayakaraṃ tu me yathā tu me na naśyeta tapas tan māṃ pracodaya
english: Agastya said: "It is exactly as you say; but it would consume my austerities. Tell me how I may act so that my austerities are not destroyed."

sanskrit: lopāmudrovāca alpāvaśiṣṭaḥ kālo 'yam ṛtau mama tapodhana na cānyathāham icchāmi tvām upaituṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Lopāmudrā said: "Very little of this season remains for me, O wealth of austerities; and I have no wish to approach you in any other manner whatsoever."

sanskrit: na cāpi dharmam icchāmi viloptuṃ te tapodhana etat tu me yathākāmaṃ saṃpādayitum arhasi
english: "Nor do I wish to infringe upon your dharma, O wealth of austerities; but this desire of mine you should fulfil."

sanskrit: agastya uvāca yady eṣa kāmaḥ subhage tava buddhyā viniścitaḥ hanta gacchāmy ahaṃ bhadre cara kāmam iha sthitā
english: Agastya said: "If this desire of yours is settled in your mind, O blessed one, then very well — I shall go and seek wealth; stay here, dear one, and let your desire abide."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tato jagāma kauravya so 'gastyo bhikṣituṃ vasu śrutarvāṇaṃ mahīpālaṃ yaṃ vedābhyadhikaṃ nṛpaiḥ
english: Lomaśa said: Then Agastya went, O Kauravya, to seek wealth — to king Śrutarvan, who surpassed other kings in knowledge of the Veda.

sanskrit: sa viditvā tu nṛpatiḥ kumbhayonim upāgamat viṣayānte sahāmātyaḥ pratyagṛhṇāt susatkṛtam
english: And the king, knowing that the jar-born one had come, went to the frontier of his realm with his ministers and received him with full honour.

sanskrit: tasmai cārghyaṃ yathānyāyam ānīya pṛthivīpatiḥ prāñjaliḥ prayato bhūtvā papracchāgamane 'rthitām
english: The lord of the earth, having brought the guest offering duly, stood with folded hands, composed, and asked the purpose of his arrival.

sanskrit: agastya uvāca vittārthinam anuprāptaṃ viddhi māṃ pṛthivīpate yathāśakty avihiṃsyānyān saṃvibhāgaṃ prayaccha me
english: Agastya said: "Know that I have come desiring wealth, O lord of the earth; share with me what you can without harming others."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tata āyavyayau pūrṇau tasmai rājā nyavedayat ato vidvann upādatsva yad atra vasu manyase
english: Lomaśa said: Then the king laid out for him his income and expenditure in full, saying: "Take from this, O learned one, whatever wealth you think fit."

sanskrit: tata āyavyayau dṛṣṭvā samau samamatir dvijaḥ sarvathā prāṇināṃ pīḍām upādānād amanyata
english: Then, seeing income and expenditure equal, the even-minded brahmin concluded that taking from it would in every way cause suffering to living beings.

sanskrit: sa śrutarvāṇam ādāya vadhryaśvam agamat tataḥ sa ca tau viṣayasyānte pratyagṛhṇād yathāvidhi
english: Taking Śrutarvan along, he then went to Vadhryaśva; and Vadhryaśva received those two at the frontier of his realm in due form.

sanskrit: tayor arghyaṃ ca pādyaṃ ca vadhryaśvaḥ pratyavedayat anujñāpya ca papraccha prayojanam upakrame
english: Vadhryaśva presented them with the guest offering and water for their feet; then, having asked leave, he inquired about their purpose at the start.

sanskrit: agastya uvāca vittakāmāv iha prāptau viddhy āvāṃ pṛthivīpate yathāśakty avihiṃsyānyān saṃvibhāgaṃ prayaccha nau
english: Agastya said: "Know that we two have come here desiring wealth, O lord of the earth; share with us what you can without harming others."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tata āyavyayau pūrṇau tābhyāṃ rājā nyavedayat tato jñātvā samādattāṃ yad atra vyatiricyate
english: Lomaśa said: Then the king laid out his income and expenditure in full before those two; knowing this, they took whatever there was in surplus.

sanskrit: tata āyavyayau dṛṣṭvā samau samamatir dvijaḥ sarvathā prāṇināṃ pīḍām upādānād amanyata
english: Then, seeing income and expenditure equal, the even-minded brahmin concluded that taking from it would in every way cause suffering to living beings.

sanskrit: paurukutsaṃ tato jagmus trasadasyuṃ mahādhanam agastyaś ca śrutarvā ca vadhryaśvaś ca mahīpatiḥ
english: Then Agastya, Śrutarvan, and king Vadhryaśva went to Trasadasyu, son of Purukutsa, who was of great wealth.

sanskrit: trasadasyuś ca tān sarvān pratyagṛhṇād yathāvidhi abhigamya mahārāja viṣayānte savāhanaḥ
english: And Trasadasyu received all of them in due form, O great king, coming to the frontier of his realm with his retinue.

sanskrit: arcayitvā yathānyāyam ikṣvākū rājasattamaḥ samāśvastāṃs tato 'pṛcchat prayojanam upakrame
english: Having honoured them duly, that best of kings of the Ikṣvāku line put them at ease and then asked their purpose at the start.

sanskrit: agastya uvāca vittakāmān iha prāptān viddhi naḥ pṛthivīpate yathāśakty avihiṃsyānyān saṃvibhāgaṃ prayaccha naḥ
english: Agastya said: "Know that we have come here desiring wealth, O lord of the earth; share with us what you can without harming others."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tata āyavyayau pūrṇau teṣāṃ rājā nyavedayat ato jñātvā samādaddhvaṃ yad atra vyatiricyate
english: Lomaśa said: Then the king laid out his income and expenditure in full before them, saying: "Knowing this, take whatever is in surplus here."

sanskrit: tata āyavyayau dṛṣṭvā samau samamatir dvijaḥ sarvathā prāṇināṃ pīḍām upādānād amanyata
english: Then, seeing income and expenditure equal, the even-minded brahmin concluded that taking from it would in every way cause suffering to living beings.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve sametyātha te nṛpās taṃ mahāmunim idam ūcur mahārāja samavekṣya parasparam
english: Then all those kings came together and, looking at one another, spoke these words to that great sage, O great king.
